experiment: bounded coalesced frame reads and exact pre-allocation outbound frame admission
decision: Accept the production implementation after full native and end-to-end gates. Experimental modes, metric fields and connection-failure stderr probes removed. No application restart or storage backend change is performed by this work.
problem: Daemon reads a complete frame through four socket reads. Every outbound frame reserves the full 8 MiB maximum before encoding, even for tiny responses, so the 128 MiB aggregate byte budget admits at most 16 concurrently blocked writers despite a probed 512-connection capacity.

root_cause.code: Writer admitted MAX_FRAME_BODY_BYTES before encoding every outbound message, regardless of actual size.

same_budget_counted.actual_body_bytes: Computed through the shared encoding operations before buffer allocation; no length-table duplicate.

root_cause.limitations: The particular earlier 32-caller RPC EOF has no recorded failure classification on its first build. Exact framing overreservation is proven independently, not asserted as the unique cause of that EOF.

implementation.byte_oracle: One FrameBodySink-based encoding operation sequence emits either real bytes or a saturating length count. Validation/counting occurs before admission and allocation. The output vector is requested at the counted length, preventing growth/reallocation while encoding.
implementation.reader: Read up to the four-byte length prefix; classify only a no-progress first-read timeout as idle. Validate length and acquire unchanged body admission before allocation. Read exactly body+four-byte CRC trailer with Take; no following frame prefetch. Preserve truncated body InvalidData vs truncated trailer UnexpectedEof, CRC validation and successful bearer-body zeroization.
implementation.lifetimes: Byte/frame guards remain live through checksum, encoding, all short/interrupted vectored writes and error returns. Frame and connection maxima, deadlines, owner/tenant admission, receipt/WAL semantics and FFI watchdog/ownership are unchanged.
implementation.allocator_example_fix: The two benchmark examples declare their own mimalloc only when the library embedded-mimalloc feature is disabled; both feature-enabled full tests and default-feature-off examples compile.

anchors.activation: Existing per-process request-profile opt-in; disabled diagnostics do not sample clocks/counters. First-byte idle waiting is excluded. These are wall spans outside the semantic dispatch ledger; they overlap and cannot be added as CPU savings.
anchors.counter_lifetime: Fixed global and seven component counter arrays, released with the process. No new resident thread/queue/pool.
anchors.reader_transient_allocation: Four fixed CRC bytes move from stack to this frame vector; at most four extra requested heap bytes per live admitted read frame, at most 256 for the unchanged 64-frame ceiling. Allocator rounding excluded.

same_binary_control.scope: Same CLI and library bytes; private actual-mode metric verified. Four processes per role/cohort, B C C B C B B C. Native C++ removes Python/GIL from timed calls. Finite strict FUSE comparisons; not SQLite dominance. P99 is mean per-leg percentile, not pooled. Daemon /proc CPU includes untimed warmup/handshakes/references and tick quantization; client CPU is measured over timed cells. Whole-daemon RSS/HWM, not isolated frame heap bytes.

final_vs_published.scope: Final production source versus accepted published source; different pinned native bytes. No private mode or setting. Source/code-layout differences remain possible; same-binary control is retained separately. Four processes per role/cohort, B C C B C B B C. Native C++ removes Python/GIL from timed calls. Finite strict FUSE comparisons; not SQLite dominance. P99 is mean per-leg percentile, not pooled. Daemon /proc CPU includes untimed warmup/handshakes/references and tick quantization; client CPU is measured over timed cells. Whole-daemon RSS/HWM, not isolated frame heap bytes.

final_32_caller_correctness.scope: Correctness/stress only; default-example/preparation checks ran concurrently. No comparative latency/CPU credit.

prototype_32_caller_checks.scope: No completed paired baseline 32-caller timing; no 32-caller speedup claim.

syscall_observer.scope: Separate strace and every-request sampling. Counts include Hello, seed, metrics, EOF and teardown. Timing under strace is never credited.

full_native.first_full_command: Failed at example compilation due to duplicate global allocators, before running suites. Fixed feature guard in the two examples; failure log retained.

gates.publication_detail: Initial combined run: 53 pass, two sub-second child-startup timeout tests fail before expected child output/PID. Those two pass in a later isolated rerun after the concurrent default example check completed; runtime preparation code is unchanged.
gates.focused: First source: 19 protocol per mode, 32 server, 14 listener. Counted source: 21 protocol per mode, 32 server, 14 listener. Full final gate supersedes these focused gates.

failed_or_incomplete_experiments: Initial discovery source_paths was called with repository rather than crate root; failed before source copying and was corrected with source fingerprint guards.
First daemon setup assumed an environment-only strict override; actual mode was Normal. Added the documented --durability strict CLI argument; failed before timed reads.

First-source baseline native32 returned short RPC read. Earlier successful cell metrics were not retained, so the incomplete run is excluded. No first-build failure-classification evidence establishes that EOF uniquely came from the frame budget.

An observer imported an executable-only benchmark controller and triggered an unintended attempt into an already existing synthetic directory. Added a __main__ guard; it failed before creating another authority.
First combined cohort reports SDK 256 KiB latency/CPU regression. The expanded unchanged-byte 16000-read cohort recovers mean/CPU but P99 still regresses 1.8%; both reports retained.
First full feature-enabled Cargo command failed before tests: examples declared duplicate global allocators. Fixed the two example feature guards and ran the complete command.
adverse_rows_and_limits: Same-byte native overlay scalar8 P99 worsens 5.5%; original SDK256K mean worsens 6.6%, client CPU 9.8%, P99 10.6%. Expanded large cohort mean improves4.1%, clientCPU2.4%, daemonCPU13.4%, but P99 worsens1.8%.
Final native overlay array1 P99 worsens7.4% despite mean improving3.2%. No universal tail improvement. All final native/SDK measured means improve, but this does not certify every workload.
Final comparison uses different binaries/source; compiler/layout effects remain possible. Matched-byte controls establish the framing algorithm separately. Shared-host activity is not isolated.

P99 values average per-leg percentiles; not pooled. Daemon CPU is /proc tick-quantized and includes warmup/reference/setup. Client CPU is timed separately. Whole-daemon RSS/HWM is not an isolated frame heap measurement.
No SQLite dominance, production application latency win or completed all-scenario objective is claimed.

runtime_verification.scope: Application readiness and native configuration verified. Published artifact hashes verified separately. No assertion that the new binary is loaded into the application, and no protected lifecycle or approval query.
